Article Title: Rahul or Vijay for PM? Congress-TVK rift talk grows after MLA’s seat shift
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay

NEW DELHI: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday after Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly.This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the state cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Speaking at an event in Kanyakumari on Saturday, Kumar said Rahul Gandhi would become the Prime Minister in 2029.The remarks came amid statements by TVK leaders projecting party chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential contender for the PM's post. TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier said the country's top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan questioned why the Congress continued to be part of the TVK government despite the differences over the prime ministerial candidate."Repeated assertions by multiple TVK Ministers even inside on the floor of the Tamil Nadu Assembly touting their leader as a probable Prime Minister is an outright rejection of the failed and dismal leadership of Rahul Gandhi by the TVK.Now, what is preventing the opportunistic Congress party from coming out of the cabinet of the TVK government? Because the TVK minister's statements are a scathing vote of no confidence, and TVK is an alliance partner, but the Congress party still continues to be in the TVK government.Why is the Congress party not withdrawing support to the TVK government after their leader Rahul Gandhi has been insulted?" news agency ANI quoted Kesavan saying.The issue has gained further attention after a private media survey placed Vijay among the preferred candidates for PM in 2029, behind PM Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi.The TVK government was formed after the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, when the party emerged as the largest force and formed the government with support from VCK, IUML, Congress, CPI and CPI(M).
Article Summary: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday. Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly. This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate.

Article Title: Haldwani ‘purification’ row: Day after FIR against Rahul, BJP, Cong trade barbs
Article Text:
BJP and Congress spar over FIR against Rahul Gandhi after his demand for action over Haldwani rally venue 'purification' remarks.

NEW DELHI: The war of words between BJP and Congress escalated Monday as the opposition party slammed the FIR against Rahul Gandhi after he demanded action over "purification" of the Haldwani rally venue as reflective of his rival's "abhorrently casteist behaviour" and BJP saying he was belatedly raking up the issue because of Mallikharjun Kharge's threat to quit as Congress chief.The sparring between the two parties came a day after Uttarakhand Police registered a case against Rahul under various BNS sections, besides SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, after the complainant, a Dalit, alleged he had given a caste angle to the cleaning work coupled with a religious ritual at Ramlila Maidan, the rally venue.Congress released a video with the title "cases are my medals" with Rahul's comments - "There are 36 cases against me. I am not afraid of Narendra Modi. But the truth is if anyone is scared, it is Modi."Senior Congress functionary Sachin Pilot asked if seeking justice is a crime. "Voice for justice cannot be suppressed under the weight of FIRs. The anti-dalit face of BJP stands exposed," he said, referring to Congress's claim that "purification" of the dais happened because Kharge, a Dalit, had addressed a meeting from it.BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said, "Rahul slept for nearly three weeks..."It seems Rahul took it up only after Kharge told him what is the point in staying in Congress when his own issue is not being raised, he added.Uttarakhand CM said people in the state are not even aware of Kharge's caste, and cited the defence of organisers, which had members from Scheduled Castes, that they cleaned the dais because it, stage for annual Ram Lila, had been left littered.

Article Title: Supreme Court slams agencies’ ‘eagerness’ to probe Abhishek’s aide
Article Text:
SC questions CBI, ED's tardiness in Leaps and Bounds probe linked to Abhishek Banerjee, seeks interrogation details by Sept 7.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday lashed out at CBI and ED for getting active in the probe against ‘Leaps and Bounds’ — a company allegedly linked to former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee’s nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee and tainted in the SSC recruitment scam — for getting huge sums from the previous TMC govt, and questioned the state police’s sudden alacrity to probe it for the same illegalities.While seeking custodial interrogation of Sumit Roy, PA to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, in the illegal sale of govt land as private property, solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned Roy’s involvement in the transfer of Rs 30 crore from a party account to Leaps and Bounds.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “The less said about Leaps and Bounds investigation, the better it is.” It noted Calcutta HC judges’ frustration over the dragging of feet by CBI and ED in investigating the firm.Mehta justified the probe, asking whether the state police should not investigate the land scam just because one agency erred. He said custodial interrogation was required as Roy was feigning lack of knowledge about the transfer of lakhs of rupees in cash.Roy’s counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan said he had mistakenly submitted during the last hearing that accused had the right to silence.He said Roy had answered questions put to him during 11 days of interrogation.Bench asked Bengal police to submit by Sept 7 details of the interrogation relating to financial transactions. It said, “When we see a case like this, the court’s job is to enable a fair investigation.” It said it wanted to examine agencies’ “eagerness” to arrest.
Article Summary: Supreme Court questions CBI, ED's tardiness in Leaps and Bounds probe linked to Abhishek Banerjee, seeks interrogation details by Sept 7. bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “The less said about Leaps & Bounds investigation, the better it is” It noted Calcutta HC judges’ frustration over the dragging of feet by CBI and ED in investigating the firm.

Article Title: 'Swachh Bharat an endeavour to reduce untouchability': Shaina NC targets Rahul Gandhi

Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC on FIR against Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC on Monday hit out at Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi after an FIR was registered against him in Uttarakhand over his remarks on an alleged purification ritual held at the venue of a Congress rally in Haldwani.“Pappu ji, the law is the same for one and all. If there is a complaint which is registered, if there is evidence which is produced, if there is an FIR, that is as per the rule book and as per the rule of law, why should there be a separate set of standards just because you're the LoP,” she said.Shaina said the SC/ST Act allows a Dalit to register a complaint based on evidence and added, “Swachh Bharat is also an endeavour to reduce untouchability in the country. You play your photo ops, we play a developmental agenda.”The FIR was registered at Kotwali police station in Haldwani under BNS Sections 196 and 299 and Section 3(1)(q) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, following a complaint alleging that Rahul Gandhi gave a caste angle to routine cleaning work carried out at Ramlila Maidan.The ritual has triggered a political row, with Congress alleging caste-based discrimination, while organisers have maintained that it was carried out to clean the venue and restore its sanctity, and denied targeting Mallikarjun Kharge on caste grounds.
Article Summary: Shaina NC hits out at Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi after an FIR was registered against him in Uttarakhand over his remarks on an alleged purification ritual held at the venue of a Congress rally. “Pappu ji, the law is the same for one and all. Article Title: 'Invoking Article 142': SC will hear Centre's plea to quash FIRs against NEET protesters on Sept 1
Article Text:
SC agrees to hear Centre's plea

SC had earlier allowed withdrawal of eligible FIRs

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear on Tuesday a plea filed by the Centre seeking to quash FIRs registered against students who participated in protests over the NEET examination paper leak.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta’s submission seeking an urgent hearing. As the bench was about to rise after the day’s proceedings, Mehta said, “We want to move an IA (interlocutory application). It’s regarding that protest for quashing of FIRs... We are invoking Article 142 (of the Constitution).”The bench observed that if the parties were reconciling the matter, it had no objection and agreed to list it for hearing on Tuesday.The Supreme Court had earlier directed that state governments were at liberty to withdraw FIRs registered against protesters involved in the nationwide demonstrations over the NEET paper leak. The court, however, clarified that those accused of grave and heinous offences would not be covered by such relief.The latest development comes as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5, accusing the Centre of failing to honour assurances made on July 25 that had led the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation over examination irregularities.According to the CJP, the march will be led by families of students who died by suicide following the cancellation of the NEET exam and subsequent re-test, as well as those who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July agitation.
Article Summary: SC had earlier allowed withdrawal of eligible FIRs against protesters. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5. The group accuses the Centre of failing to honour assurances made on July 25 that had led the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation.

Article Title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs
Article Text:
TMC rebel MPs after attending the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) Parliamentary Party Meeting (ANI photo)

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI and sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that lays down the anti-defection framework.Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.In a post on X, TMC Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra shared the photo of one of the notices issued to rebel MPs and said, “Cover up caught out!” Highlighting that TMC had filed 20 disqualification petitions in June, Moitra said, “Speaker LS did nothing except give them better seats at our expense. SG Tushar Mehta in Court said the Speaker had issued notices. Notice dated Aug 25th -- exact date of hearing!”On Tuesday, Supreme Court sought a response from Lok Sabha Speaker’s office on time-bound adjudication of TMC’s petition seeking disqualification of rebel MPs who broke away from the party after its electoral debacle in West Bengal, even as Abhishek Banerjee accused Speaker Om Birla of “deliberate inaction”.The SC also issued notices to the 20 rebel MPs: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachna Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Abu Teher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Kalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.In his petition, Abhishek Banerjee told the court on Tuesday that he had lodged the disqualification petition against the rebel MPs on June 18 and complained that despite the lapse of two months, no meaningful progress has been made on its adjudication.The continuing delay in the adjudication process is impacting democratic governance, he said.In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June. Banerjee had earlier met Birla on July 27 in Parliament urging him to expedite his decision on the pending petitions.
Article Summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI. The notices sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification.

Article Title: Doctor who attempted suicide at Sion station dies four days later in hospital, FIR registered
Article Text: Mumbai: Four days after attempting suicide at Sion railway station, a 28-year-old medical officer serving in Satara’s Phaltan died at Sion Hospital on Monday. While the exact circumstances of the incident remain unclear, BMC Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (BMC-MARD) stated that Dr Rajendra Rupnavar (the deceased) faced alleged workplace harassment and undue external or political pressure.Dadar Govt Railway Police (GRP) is in the process of registering an FIR for ‘abetment of suicide’, based on a complaint given by Rupnavar’s family. The case will be transferred to Phaltan for further investigation.On Aug 27, Rupnavar had climbed a telecom tower and attempted to hang himself at Sion railway station around 7.45 am. Someone informed the GRP who summoned the fire brigade. Despite repeated appeals by the police, he refused to come down from the tower and tied a noose around his neck. Firefighters soon brought him down and rushed him to Sion Hospital.Last year, a 28-year-old medical officer at the Phaltan Sub-District Hospital died by suicide after being repeatedly raped by a police sub-inspector.Need help? Contact: MPower Mental Health Helpline 1800-120-820050
Article Summary: Dr Rajendra Rupnavar, 28, was a medical officer serving in Satara’s Phaltan. He faced alleged workplace harassment and undue external or political pressure. He had climbed a telecom tower and attempted to hang himself at Sion railway station.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: 3,400 SIR forms found at Navi Mumbai photocopy shop; 5 BLOs suspended as Sena (UBT)-BJP clash
Article Text:
Authorities seized numerous printed Special Intensive Revision forms from the premises

THANE/MUMBAI: Five Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were suspended after 3,400 enumeration forms related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls were found at a private photocopy shop in Navi Mumbai’s Kharghar, triggering a political confrontation between Shiv Sena (UBT) and BJP workers and prompting an administrative inquiry, police and district officials said.The forms, which were filled by voters from the Panvel Assembly constituency, were found at a photocopy centre in Sector 19 following complaints that SIR applications were being photocopied there and that a person associated with the BJP youth wing was allegedly in unauthorised possession of them.Police rushed to the shop and took Suraj Patil, who was allegedly getting the forms photocopied, into custody.Authorities also seized thousands of printed SIR forms from the premises and shifted them to the police station, news agency PTI reported.he controversy came to light after a video related to the incident went viral on Thursday.The administration subsequently ordered an inquiry into how forms filled by voters reached a private photocopy centre.Following the complaint, the Electoral Registration Officer deputed Assistant Electoral Registration Officers to inspect the photocopy centre.During the inspection, officials found that Patil had brought 3,400 applications to the shop.Scrutiny showed that the forms belonged to 11 polling stations. A majority of the applications were from five polling stations, while single copies were found from six other polling stations.Shiv Sena (UBT) workers had confronted Patil at the shop, alleging that he was a BJP Youth Wing office-bearer. BJP workers, however, denied any connection with the matter.Sena (UBT) workers also alleged that Patil managed to flee the Kharghar police station shortly after being taken there for questioning.Raigad district collector Kishan Jawale on Friday said a case had been registered against Patil under the Representation of the People Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Jawale visited the office of Panvel Sub-Divisional Officer Pawan Chandak and said the five BLOs had been suspended pending disciplinary proceedings.Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer Balesh Bhojane questioned how SIR forms filled by ordinary voters could have reached private individuals and alleged that BJP youth wing functionaries were linked to the incident.Panvel Municipal Corporation mayor and BJP leader Nitin Patil, however, said party workers had no connection with the matter.Opposition NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said suspending the five BLOs was not enough and alleged that the incident exposed problems in the way the SIR process was being conducted."We have been saying that the BJP is using this process to ensure its poll victory and this incident proves us right," he said.Pawar said he had sought a response from the Election Commission over the incident, but the authorities had passed the responsibility to the Election Commission of India."Suspending only the BLOs is not enough. The authorities who instructed them should also be suspended, and action should be taken against the BJP workers involved," Pawar added.He also said there could be many similar incidents that had not been detected and sought a response from the Election Commission.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: 5 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) suspended after 3,400 enumeration forms found at private photocopy shop in Navi Mumbai’s Kharghar. Police took Suraj Patil, who was allegedly getting the forms photocopied, into custody. Authorities also seized thousands of printed SIR forms from the premises.

Article Title: Conman fools 79-yr-old man, flees with gold chain & ring worth Rs1.5L

A conman allegedly distracted a 79-year-old man and fled with his gold chain and ring worth Rs1.5 lakh in Chakan around 10am on Sunday. Article Title: Bangladeshi couple convicted for illegal stay
Article Text:
Nagpur:





District and sessions judge KH Thombre on Monday convicted a Bangladeshi couple for illegally residing in India and sentenced them to the period the husband and wife have already spent in jail.Mohammad Lahu Mohammad Ayub Sheikh and his wife were found guilty under Section 14-A(B) of the Foreigners Act, 1946, and Section 6 of the Passport (Entry into India) Rules, 1950.The court recorded that the woman had undergone imprisonment of 2 years, 5 months and 10 days, while her husband had served 2 years, 5 months and 8 days. Both were fined Rs10,000 each, with 15 days’ simple imprisonment in default. The sentences will run concurrently.Prison authorities were directed to send both accused to Bangladesh after they complete the sentence and pay the fine.The case stems from the detection branch raid on April 13, 2024, at a lodge on Itgaon Phata–Khaparkheda–Parseoni road under Parseoni police station limits after a tip-off about flesh trade.Probe showed the couple had entered and stayed in India without valid documents. A case was registered under the Foreigners Act, Passport Rules and relevant BNS sections.Public prosecutor Ram Anwane examined eight witnesses. Illegal residence was proved, but the court acquitted the couple of forgery. Prison authorities were directed to send both accused to Bangladesh after they complete the sentence and pay the fine.
Article Summary: Mohammad Lahu Mohammad Ayub Sheikh and his wife were found guilty under Section 14-A(B) of the Foreigners Act, 1946. Both were fined Rs10,000 each, with 15 days’ simple imprisonment in default. Prison authorities were directed to send both accused to Bangladesh after they complete the sentence and pay the fine.

Article Title: No more phones at temples in TN, secure counters set up
Article Text: CHENNAI: Devotees visiting major temples across Tamil Nadu will have to deposit their mobile phones at designated counters before entering the premises from September 1. Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department has directed temple authorities to ensure their safe custody and return.The move is aimed at protecting the sanctity of temples and preventing photography, videography and social-media reels inside temple premises. Devotees will be charged ₹5 per phone and issued a receipt. Temples have been instructed to deploy employees or volunteers to receive, secure and return the devices, while maintaining records of phones deposited and returned.Temple staff have also been directed to prevent unauthorised recording. Photography and videography involving VIPs and dignitaries will require permission.Meanwhile, during the question hour in the assembly on Monday, HR&CE minister C Ramesh said the govt is studying queue management systems at major temples. He said a revamp of entry and exit routes at major temples is also on the anvil to ease overcrowding and ensure devotees can have darshan without obstruction.He also said the preparations for the 2028 Mahamaham festival in Kumbakonam has begun. A review meeting involving officials of various departments had been held through the district collector.
Article Summary: Devotees visiting major temples across Tamil Nadu will have to deposit their mobile phones at designated counters. The move is aimed at protecting the sanctity of temples and preventing photography, videography and social-media reels inside temple premises. Devotees will be charged ₹5 per phone and issued a receipt.

Article Title: Vaiko backs Rahul as PM candidate; Tagore, Praveen Chakravarthy meet Vijay
Article Text:
Tagore, Chakravarthy meet CM

Chennai:





A day after Tamil Nadu tourism minister R Rajesh Kumar warned that Congress would pull its two ministers out of the state cabinet if TVK failed to accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha election, the ruling party chose not to respond publicly. Meanwhile, TNCC president Manickam Tagore and Congress MP Praveen Chakravarthy separately met chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday. TVK’s silence and the visit of Congress leaders signalled an effort by both sides to defuse the situation.Manickam Tagore said in an X post that not all surveys reflect public sentiment, a reference to the survey by a media house that said Vijay was third most popular PM candidate in the country next to PM Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi. “Sometimes, numbers shown as voice of people are weapons intended to split people,’’ he said. Narrating a short story titled ‘a fox’s fake survey,’ Tagore said there are attempts to drive wedge between two friends through ‘fabricated numbers. ’Speaking at a public meeting in Kanyakumari on Sunday, Rajesh Kumar said Rahul Gandhi would be Congress’s prime ministerial candidate in 2029. He said the two Congress ministers in Tamil Nadu cabinet would quit if TVK refused to accept Rahul as PM candidate.The statement was a result of TVK ministers projecting Vijay as prospective PM candidate.On Monday, MDMK general secretary Vaiko joined the debate, backing Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate and urging Vijay to restrain TVK ministers.“Congress party leads INDIA bloc at the national level. Therefore, Rahul Gandhi is the only viable PM candidate from the alliance. There is simply no alternative,’’ he told reporters in Tirunelveli. Vaiko said Vijay would not have such aspirations and that it was the TVK ministers who were making remarks projecting Vijay as the PM candidate.“Ministers should not speak haphazardly about these matters. CM must direct the ministers to avoid such statements in the future,” said Vaiko.Meanwhile, Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was allotted front row among leaders of opposition parties triggering speculation it was a fallout of Rajesh Kumar’s speech. However, Tagore clarified in a statement that it was a routine administrative exercise after her election as the party’s legislative leader. Speaker J C D Prabhakar also clarified that Cuthbert was allotted the seat because of her designation as floor leader.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu tourism minister R Rajesh Kumar warned that Congress would pull its two ministers out of the state cabinet if TVK failed to accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha election. The ruling party chose not to respond publicly. Meanwhile, TNCC president Manickam Tagore and Congress MP Praveen Chakravarthy separately met chief minister C Joseph Vijay.

Article Title: Three ambulance drivers arrested for cutting birthday cakes with machete near Pollachi
Article Text:
Suresh celebrated his birthday on Thursday night with his friends near the CTC Medu new bus stand. They placed two cakes on a stretcher used for transporting patients and cut them with a machete.





COIMBATORE: The Mahalingapuram police in Coimbatore district have arrested three ambulance drivers for celebrating the birthday of one of them by cutting two cakes with a machete near the CTC Medu bus stand on the Pollachi–Coimbatore Road.The arrested have been identified as Suresh, 35, Vanjinathan, 32 and Vengadesan, 30, of Pollachi.Suresh celebrated his birthday on Thursday night with his friends near the CTC Medu new bus stand. They placed two cakes on a stretcher used for transporting patients and cut them with a machete.The video of the incident surfaced online, triggering widespread outrage and concern. Following this, the Mahalingapuram police registered a case and arrested the three men who were in the video.Police seized the machete used for cutting the cakes. The arrested men were remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Suresh celebrated his birthday on Thursday night with his friends near the CTC Medu new bus stand. They placed two cakes on a stretcher used for transporting patients and cut them with a machete. The video of the incident surfaced online, triggering widespread outrage and concern.

Article Title: Farmer abducted from Hosur
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: A farmer was abducted by two men who arrived in a car near his house at Kelamangalam in Hosur on Friday night. Police have registered a case and launched an intensive hunt.The abducted farmer has been identified as Gopal,58, of Anusoni village near Kelamangalam.According to sources, two unidentified men arrived near Gopal’s house in a car bearing a Kerala registration number around 7 pm on Friday. They called him out of his residence under the pretext of striking up a conversation. Moments later, the duo forcibly pushed Gopal into the vehicle and sped away.The incident was captured on a nearby CCTV camera. Gopal’s wife retrieved the footage and lodged a formal complaint at the Kelamangalam police station.Based on her complaint, police opened an investigation to determine the motive behind the abduction. A special police team has been formed to rescue Gopal and apprehend the culprits.
Article Summary: The abducted farmer has been identified as Gopal,58, of Anusoni village near Kelamangalam. Two unidentified men arrived near Gopal’s house in a car bearing a Kerala registration number. They called him out of his residence under the pretext of striking up a conversation. Moments later, they forcibly pushed Gopal into the vehicle and sped away.

Article Title: Thoothukudi firing: Will TVK govt reopen cases against 3 top officials?
Article Text:
file picture





Madurai: Madras high court on Monday sought the TVK govt’s stand on re-examining the decisions taken by the previous govt to drop disciplinary action against three officials -- the then Thoothukudi district collector N Venkatesh, then inspector-general of police Shailesh Kumar Yadav and then DIG of police Kapil Kumar C Saratkar -- in connection with the police firing on anti-Sterlite protestors in Thoothukudi in 2018.Pursuant to the earlier order, the state filed a compliance report before the court stating that it was under the previous DMK govt further action was dropped in the disciplinary proceedings initiated against the three officials. Taking into account the report, a division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel sought response from the present TVK govt with regard to re-examining the decisions taken by the previous govt to drop the disciplinary action.Earlier, the court directed the state to file detailed reports on documents relating to Justice Aruna Jagadeesan Commission, action taken on the commission’s report and relief granted to the family members of the victims.The court passed the order while hearing a batch of petitions filed in 2018 pertaining to the Tuticorin police firing incident. The petitioners sought a direction to initiate action against the erring officials responsible for the death of 13 people in the incident. The matter was adjourned to Sept 10.
Article Summary: Madras high court sought TVK govt’s stand on re-examining the decisions taken by the previous govt to drop disciplinary action against three officials. The three officials were involved in the police firing on anti-Sterlite protestors in Thoothukudi in 2018.

Article Title: Father, son held for harassment of 14-year-old girl in Madurai
Article Text: Madurai: Tallakulam all-woman police on Monday arrested a father and son on charges of harassing a 14-year-old schoolgirl.The accused were Boominathan, 57, and Sankarapandian, 30. Police said the girl was a neighbour of the accused, and she was on her way to school when the duo allegedly caught hold of her hand and pulled her. They allegedly behaved inappropriately with the girl, police said.Following a complaint from the girl's parent, police registered a case under relevant sections of Pocso Act and BNS and arrested them.
Article Summary: The accused were Boominathan, 57, and Sankarapandian, 30. Police said the girl was a neighbour of the accused. She was on her way to school when the duo allegedly caught hold of her hand and pulled her.

Article Title: Congress minister threatens to quit TVK cabinet if Rahul not accepted as PM candidate in 2029
Article Text: MADURAI: Signalling a fresh strain in the ruling coalition, Congress leader and Tamil Nadu tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar threatened to quit the state cabinet if TVK refuses to accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate in 2029 Lok Sabha elections.“Rahul Gandhi will be the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 parliamentary election. He will become the next PM. If at all TVK refuses the accept this, the two Congress ministers will walk out of the cabinet,” Rajesh Kumar said on Sunday at the swearing in ceremony of George Robinson as Congress party’s Kanyakumari West district unit. "For us, party is above all other considerations. Our cadres want to see Rahul Gandhi as PM. Our goal is to achieve that,’’ he said.The remark comes against the backdrop of repeated attempts by TVK leaders to project chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential prime ministerial face from Tamil Nadu in 2029.The issue was first raised by PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna during a debate on delimitation exercise when he said a Prime Minister should emerge from Tamil Nadu. His remarks were followed by other TVK ministers, including D Sarathkumar, A Srinath and K Jagadeeswari, projecting Vijay as a possible prime ministerial candidate.The debate gained traction nationally after a private media house said their survey has found Vijay was the third most preferred prime ministerial choice in the country, following Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi.The statements by TVK leaders sparked unease among the Congress rank and file. When asked about the issue, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore took a swipe at TVK ministers, saying they were still functioning with a “fan club mindset.”Rajesh Kumar’s warning, however, marks an escalation of the disagreement. The support of five MLAs of Congress remains crucial for TVK to enjoy the majority mark in the state assembly. In return, TVK has given two ministerial berths to Congress leaders Rajesh Kumar and Viswanathan. Earlier in the day, Viswanathan too said Rahul Gandhi was their PM candidate and there would be no change in the stand.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar threatened to quit the state cabinet if TVK refuses to accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate in 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The remark comes against the backdrop of repeated attempts by TVK leaders to project chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential prime ministerial face from Tamil Nadu. The support of five MLAs of Congress remains crucial for TVK to enjoy the majority mark.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.

Article Title: Excise officer arrested in Pocso case in Mundakkayam
Article Text:
The accused was identified as Arun Kumar (46) of Punchavayal

Kottayam

:





Mundakkayam police on Monday arrested an excise officer in connection with the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl.The accused was identified as Arun Kumar (46) of Punchavayal. Article Title: DGP’s foreign visit: Kerala HC seeks documents within 10 days
Article Text:
DGP S Sreejith

Kochi

:





The high court has directed the additional chief secretary of the home department and the vigilance director to produce within 10 days, in a sealed cover, the documents based on which they decided that no inquiry was needed into the allegation that DGP S Sreejith had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad.A bench of Justice A Badharudeen issued the order on a petition filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Kannur, seeking a vigilance inquiry into the allegation. According to the petitioner, Sreejith, while serving as the transport commissioner, had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad while wearing his police uniform.Previously, following a court directive, the additional chief secretary had considered the petitioner’s complaint, along with the documents he had submitted, and decided that no vigilance inquiry was warranted into the complaint for the time being. Subsequently, the petitioner approached the court challenging the clean chit given by the vigilance department to Sreejith.During the hearing on Monday, the govt pleader sought additional time to file an objection to the petition. Meanwhile, the petitioner alleged that the clean chit had been given to Sreejith without a proper inquiry. He further sought a directive to the vigilance department to produce, in a sealed cover, the documents on which it had based its decision not to conduct an inquiry into the matter, for the perusal of the court. Accordingly, the court directed that the documents be produced in a sealed cover and adjourned the matter to Sept 7.
Article Summary: Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Kannur, sought a vigilance inquiry into the allegation. According to the petitioner, Sreejith, while serving as the transport commissioner, had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad while wearing his police uniform.

Article Title: Muttil tree felling: Cheating case posted to Sept 7
Article Text:
Muttil tree felling

Kochi:





Chottanikkara judicial first class magistrate court on Monday dismissed the petition filed by the accused in the cheating case connected with the controversial tree felling at Muttil in Wayanad in 2020-21. The court posted the framing of charges against the accused to Sept 7.The court on Monday heard a petition filed by the accused seeking a stay on further proceedings in the case, but dismissed it. The court, however, allowed the petition filed by the first accused Roji Augustine to record his plea through video conferencing. His brothers Josekutty and Anto Augustine had earlier filed similar pleas which were also allowed.Kerala High Court had earlier dismissed a petition filed by Roji, seeking a stay of the ongoing trial in the cheating case in Chottanikkara court.The case pertains to the FIR registered by Ambalamedu police on a petition filed by M M Aliyar, proprietor of Malabar Timber Industries, Karimugal. Aliyar had alleged fraud in the sale of timber from the illegally felled trees in 2021. In July, HC dismissed the discharge petitions filed by Josekutty and Anto. The allegation is that they cheated Aliyar of Rs 1.4 crore and the FIR was registered on July 13, 2021.The illegal felling of rosewood trees on revenue patta lands of Muttil South village allegedly occurred in Nov-Dec 2020 and Jan-Feb 2021. The three brothers are the key accused in the case.
Article Summary: The court posted the framing of charges against the accused to Sept 7. The case pertains to the FIR registered by Ambalamedu police on a petition filed by M M Aliyar, proprietor of Malabar Timber Industries, Karimugal. In July, HC dismissed the discharge petitions filed by Josekutty and Anto.
